observation.visible_scene: A macro close-up of a transparent liquid splash crown — a rounded droplet mass at the lower center with an upward crown of thin liquid ligaments and a horizontal band of tiny droplets — set against a dark, granular, out-of-focus background containing scattered bokeh highlights and a few fixed bright filament-like reflections (a curved strand at left, a faint purple strand at upper right, a short vertical streak at top). The framing and the background filaments stay in essentially the same positions throughout, indicating a static camera; the visible change is confined to the liquid structure itself.
visible_changes: The upper spike/ligament of the crown progressively tilts and curves to the right over the excerpt: in the early frames it is fairly compact and near-vertical, by the middle frames it forms a rightward-leaning hook, and by the late frames it leans further right with a small curled tip.
The central horizontal band of small droplets/ligaments continuously reshapes, becoming more jagged and reorganizing rather than translating as a rigid body.

New thin ligaments emerge during the segment: a more vertical branching ligament develops on the left side of the crown (becoming prominent in the latter half), and a short downward drip/ligament forms at the bottom edge of the rounded droplet mass near the end of the clip.
The rounded bottom droplet mass remains roughly stationary in position, with only its outline and internal highlights subtly deforming.
Overall the crown appears to deform and reconfigure slowly (tilting/rotating its upper part rightward and growing new ligaments), not as a rapid expansion or a clear translation of the whole object.
Background bokeh and the fixed bright filaments show no consistent positional change, supporting that the observed motion belongs to the liquid, not the camera.
outside_clip_unknowns: The cause or onset of the splash (no impact or trigger is shown within the excerpt).
Whether the liquid motion is real high-speed footage or a render/simulation.
The continuation of the deformation beyond the last frame and what preceded the first frame (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
The true 3D orientation and depth of the crown relative to the camera.
uncertain_details: Exact direction and magnitude of the upper-spike rotation vs. simple deformation are hard to disambiguate from sampled frames.
Minor apparent shifts in background highlights could be focus/reflection flicker rather than object motion; treated as static.
Whether the emerging left ligament and bottom drip are new structures or previously hidden parts becoming visible is not determinable.
The horizontal band's changes could be a mix of droplet coalescence, stretching, and viewpoint-dependent refraction; not separable here.

may already be underway in the first view and may continue beyond the last. The endpoints need
NOT match or connect as a loop. Do not judge different endpoints as a physical inconsistency,
and do not invent a trigger, contact, start, stop, landing, disappearance or completion to make
the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.
If an editing cut is visible inside the segment, distinguish it from continuous physical motion;
do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.
Describe what is visible during the excerpt, the actual changes, and supported persistent
properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;
do not invent causes, an earlier impact, an unseen operator, material identities or later outcomes.
Do not infer motion from one frame, a visible seam or a single pose. Static intervals are valid.
Do not supply named physics laws. Compare each important entity's first and last image positions
and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
